summary: Masao Abe was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University, Kyoto University, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia University, working under Hajime Tanabe, Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, Keiji Nishitani, Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Reinhold Niebuhr, and Paul Tillich.

Masao Shizutani specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He held posts as an assistant professor at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested in 1974).
Masaru Akimoto works in the fields of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held positions at Kyoto Women's University, where he is attested in 2002 as a professor and again in 2015.

Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He held multiple academic posts at Komazawa University, including lecturer (1984), associate professor (1988, 1994), professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019).

Masataka Suzuki is a scholar of religious studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at Keio University (~1968–1978), he held a post there (~1984–2015), and is attested as a lecturer at ICPBS and IIBS in 2026.

Masataro Sawayanagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1886–1888). Over his career, he held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1897–1898), Tohoku University (~1911–1913), Taisho University (~1926–1927), and Kyushu University.

Masato Kobayashi is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, later serving as a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2002–2006).

Masatoshi Konishi was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who studied at International Christian University, the University of Calcutta, the University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University. He served at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as an instructor of Sanskrit at Harvard University beginning in 1958.

Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1980). He held posts at Kyoto Tachibana University (~1984–1989), Kansai University (~1989–1993), and Osaka University (~1993–2017).

Masayuki Tsukimoto works in the fields of Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Massimo Pallottino was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1927–1931), later holding posts at the University of Cagliari (~1940–1945) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1945–1980).

Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He has held positions at Minobusan University, attested as a lecturer in 2001, a professor in 2015, and a specially appointed professor in 2026.
Mathew Varghese is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post as a research fellow in 2012 and as a lecturer attested in 2026 at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Mathieu Beaudouin specializes in linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology, having studied at Panthéon-Sorbonne University and INALCO. His teaching posts include INALCO, EPHE, and a 2025 British Academy International Fellowship at the University of Cambridge.

Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He founded and, beginning in 1992, held a professorship at the Université du Québec à Montréal.
Mathilde Deromps was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Jules Bloch between 1911 and 1914.

Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze was a scholar in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Indology. In 1697, he was librarian at Humboldt University of Berlin, and served as librarian and antiquary at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1697–1739).

Matteo Bartoli was a linguist who studied under Heinrich Hübschmann and Michele Kerbaker at the universities of Vienna, Strasbourg, and Paris. He later taught at the University of Pisa (1907–1908) and was professor of linguistics at the University of Turin (1908–1946).

Matthew Atmore Sherring was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Coward College (~1845–1849) and University College London (1848–1850). In 1852, he took up a post as a missionary for the London Missionary Society.
